security.title: Security
security.signed-out-others: All other devices are signed out.
security.not-found: That device was already signed out.
security.passkeys-intro: A passkey signs you in with your fingerprint, your face or your device’s screen lock, with nothing to type.
security.passkey-head: As a head of a household, you need two factors to sign in. Add another passkey first, then you can remove this one.
security.passkey-failed: Adding the passkey didn’t work. Try again, or add it on another device.
security.confirm-intro: You signed in more than 10 minutes ago. Confirm it’s you to change how you sign in.
security.passkey-confirm-failed: Confirming with a passkey didn’t work. Try again, or enter your password.
security.confirmed: Confirmed. For the next 10 minutes, you can change how you sign in.
security.incorrect-code: The code from your authenticator app is incorrect. Enter the newest one it shows.
security.two-factor-intro: After your password, signing in also asks for a code from an authenticator app on your phone. Then your password alone isn’t enough for anyone else to sign in.
security.setup-scan: Scan this QR code with your authenticator app.
security.setup-qr: QR code to set up your authenticator app
security.setup-key: Can’t scan it? Enter this key in the app instead:
security.setup-code-hint: The six digits the app now shows for Householdr.
security.setup-incorrect: The code is incorrect. Enter the newest code the app shows for Householdr.
security.setup-not-started: There’s no setup to finish. Start turning it on again.
security.two-factor-head: As a head of a household, you need two factors to sign in. Add a passkey first, then you can turn two-factor authentication off.
security.two-factor-already-off: Two-factor authentication is off, so there are no recovery codes to replace.
security.recovery-codes-intro: If you can’t use your authenticator app, sign in with one of these codes instead. Each works once. Keep them somewhere safe, such as your password manager: this is the only time they are shown.
security.recovery-codes-made: New recovery codes are made. The old ones no longer work.
email.password-reset.subject: Choose a new password for Householdr
email.password-reset.request: Someone asked to reset the password of your Householdr account.
email.password-reset.expiry: The link works once, within 30 minutes.
email.password-reset.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then ignore this e-mail: your password stays as it is.
email.password-changed.subject: Your Householdr password was changed
email.password-changed.done: The password of your Householdr account was just changed, and every device was signed out.
email.password-changed.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then someone else can read your e-mail. Secure your e-mail account first, then choose a new password with “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page.
email.passkey-added.subject: A passkey was added to your Householdr account
email.passkey-added.done: A passkey was just added to your Householdr account. It signs in to your account without your password.
email.passkey-added.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then someone else is signed in to your account. On the security page, remove the passkey and sign out all other devices, then choose a new password with “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page.
email.passkey-removed.subject: A passkey was removed from your Householdr account
email.passkey-removed.done: A passkey was just removed from your Householdr account. It no longer signs in.
email.passkey-removed.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then someone else is signed in to your account. On the security page, sign out all other devices, then choose a new password with “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page.
email.two-factor-on.subject: Two-factor authentication was turned on for your Householdr account
email.two-factor-on.done: Two-factor authentication was just turned on for your Householdr account. Signing in with your password now also asks for a code from your authenticator app, or one of your recovery codes.
email.two-factor-on.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then someone else is signed in to your account. On the security page, sign out all other devices and turn two-factor authentication off, then choose a new password with “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page.
email.two-factor-off.subject: Two-factor authentication was turned off for your Householdr account
email.two-factor-off.done: Two-factor authentication was just turned off for your Householdr account. Your password signs you in on its own again.
email.two-factor-off.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then someone else is signed in to your account. On the security page, sign out all other devices, then choose a new password with “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page and turn two-factor authentication on again.
email.recovery-codes-changed.subject: New recovery codes were made for your Householdr account
email.recovery-codes-changed.done: New recovery codes were just made for your Householdr account. The old ones no longer work.
email.recovery-codes-changed.not-you: Wasn’t it you? Then someone else is signed in to your account. On the security page, sign out all other devices, then choose a new password with “Forgot your password?” on the sign-in page.
sign-in.password-changed: Your password is changed. Sign in with the new one.
forgot.title: Forgot your password?
forgot.intro: Enter the e-mail address of your account, and we’ll send you a link to choose a new password.
forgot.sent: If {email} has an account, we’ve sent it a link to choose a new password. The link works once, within 30 minutes.
forgot.invalid: Enter an e-mail address, like name@example.org.
reset.title: Choose a new password
reset.hint: At least 12 characters, and no other rules.
reset.breached: This password appeared in a data breach elsewhere, so others may try it. Choose another one.
reset.expired: This link has expired or was used already.
reset.code: Code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code
reset.recovery-code-hint: Without the app, enter one of the recovery codes you saved when you turned on two-factor authentication, such as abcde-12345. Each works once.
reset.needs-code: Enter the code from your authenticator app, or a recovery code.
reset.incorrect-code: The code is incorrect, or it was used already. Enter the newest code your app shows, or another recovery code.

match.countPlural=one: After several wrong codes, this pauses for a moment. You can try again in {count} second.
match.countPlural=other: After several wrong codes, this pauses for a moment. You can try again in {count} seconds.

match.countPlural=one: After several wrong codes, this pauses for a moment. You can try again in {count} minute.

sign-in-code.title: Two-factor authentication
sign-in-code.intro: Enter the code your authenticator app shows for Householdr.
sign-in-code.recovery-code-hint: One of the codes you saved when you turned on two-factor authentication, such as abcde-12345. Each works once.
sign-in-code.recovery-submit: Sign in with the recovery code
sign-in-code.incorrect: The code is incorrect. Enter the newest code your app shows.
sign-in-code.incorrect-recovery: The recovery code is incorrect, or it was used already.
sign-in-code.expired: Signing in took longer than 10 minutes. Start again with your password.

sign-up.intro: First, confirm your e-mail address: we’ll send you a link to continue.
sign-up.sent: If {email} has no account yet, we’ve sent it a link to continue. The link works for 30 minutes.
sign-up.invalid: Enter an e-mail address, like name@example.org.
sign-up.wait: Many sign-ups came from your network in the last hour. Try again later.
sign-up.have-account: Already have an account? Sign in
household-setup.title: Set up your household
household-setup.expired: This link has expired or was used already.
household-setup.intro: Tell us about your household and about you. You can change these details later.
household-setup.language-hint: Whoever you invite starts with this language, and can choose their own.
household-setup.read-terms: Read the terms (opens in a new tab)
household-setup.passkey: You’ll sign in with a passkey: your fingerprint, your face or your device’s screen lock, with nothing to type.
household-setup.create: Create the household with a passkey
household-setup.unsupported: Creating a household needs a passkey, which this browser can’t make. Open the link from the e-mail in an up-to-date browser, with JavaScript on.
household-setup.not-created: Nothing was created. Try again, and allow the passkey when your device asks.
household-setup.invalid-name: Enter the household’s name, up to 100 characters.
household-setup.invalid-time-zone: Choose one of the country’s time zones.
household-setup.invalid-week-start: Choose the day weeks start on.
household-setup.invalid-head-name: Enter your name, up to 100 characters.
household-setup.invalid-adult: Only someone 18 or older can create a household.
household-setup.invalid-terms: Accept the terms to create a household.

email.sign-up.request: Someone asked to create a household on Householdr with this e-mail address.

home.none: You’re not in a household yet.
home.invitation: When someone invites you to their household, open the link they send you to join it.
household.head: Head
household.add-adult-intro: Add the other adults who live here, so they share the chores too. Each of them can join with an account of their own later.
household.name: Name
household.added: {name} is added. Let them know: once they join with an account of their own, they can see everything recorded about them.
household.invalid-name: Enter their name, up to 100 characters.
household.link-help: Send this link to {name}. It works once, for 7 days. Whoever opens it can join as {name}, so send it to them only.

match.countPlural=other: An invitation link is out. It works for {count} more days.

household.revoked: {name}’s link is revoked: it no longer works.
household.not-invitable: That profile can’t be invited any more. It may have joined already.
invitation.title: Join {household}
invitation.invited: You’re invited to join {household} on Householdr as {profile}.
invitation.sign-in-first: Sign in to accept, or create an account to join.
invitation.not-allowed: Confirm your e-mail address first: joining a household needs it.
invitation.expired: This invitation has expired or was used already. Ask whoever invited you for a new link.
invitation.confirmed: Your e-mail address {email} is confirmed. Create your account to join.
invitation.passkey: You’ll sign in with a passkey: your fingerprint, your face or your device’s screen lock, with nothing to type.
invitation.join-with-passkey: Create my account with a passkey and join
invitation.unsupported: Creating an account needs a passkey, which this browser can’t make. Open the links again in an up-to-date browser, with JavaScript on.
invitation.not-created: Nothing was created. Try again, and allow the passkey when your device asks.
invitation.sign-up-expired: The link that confirmed your e-mail address has expired or was used already.
invitation.invalid-name: Enter your name, up to 100 characters.
invitation.invalid-terms: Accept the terms to create an account.
household.share-text: Here’s your invitation to join {household} on Householdr, where we share the chores fairly.
household.qr-help: Or let {name} scan this code with their phone’s camera.
household.qr: QR code of the invitation link for {name}
household.add-child-intro: Only someone with parental responsibility for a child can add them. If you don’t have it, as a step-parent may not, invite one of the child’s parents to add them instead.
household.child-consent: I have parental responsibility for this child, and I agree to them using Householdr.
household.child-added: {name} is added. Let them know, in words they understand: once they have an account of their own, they can see everything recorded about them.
household.invalid-birth-date: Enter their birth date, no later than today.
household.child-is-adult: They’re 18 or older: add them as an adult instead.
household.invalid-consent: To add a child, confirm that you have parental responsibility for them and agree to them using Householdr.
settings.title: Household settings
settings.country-hint: The country sets the age from which a child can have an account of their own.
settings.logged: The activity log shows every member which settings you change.
settings.conflict: {name} changed these settings a moment ago, so yours weren’t saved. Your changes are still in the form: compare them with the settings now, then save again.
settings.conflict-someone: Someone changed these settings a moment ago, so yours weren’t saved. Your changes are still in the form: compare them with the settings now, then save again.
activity.title: Activity
activity.intro: What was done that affects others in the household. Everyone in the household sees it, and nobody can change or delete it.

match.who=you: You changed the household’s time zone.

time-zone.name: {city} ({zone})
shares.title: Shares
shares.intro: A share sets how much of the household’s work someone does, compared with the others. Adults have a full share. Children have a share by their age: none under 4, a tenth at 4, growing to a full share at 18.
shares.private-heads: Only the heads, each member themselves and a child’s parents in the household see a share. Everyone sees the balances, which take shares into account.
shares.private: Only you and the household’s heads see your share. A head can change it.
shares.private-child: Only you, the household’s heads and your parents in it see your share. A head can change it.
shares.set: {share} this week, set by a head
shares.hint: A whole number from {min} to {max}. 100 is a full adult share, not all the work: shares are compared with each other, so two members at 100 do the same amount. Someone with 0 gets no tasks.
shares.invalid: Enter a whole number from {min} to {max}.
shares.conflict: {name} changed a moment ago, so your change wasn’t saved. Their share is {share} this week. What you entered is still in the form, so you can save it again.
shares.temporary-this-week: {share} this week, with a temporary share
shares.temporary-hint: On the days you choose, both included, it replaces the share. It can start this week, and up to a year ahead. No reason is asked or kept.
shares.check-temporary: Check the temporary share you entered.
shares.invalid-last-day: Choose a day from the first day to {latest}.
shares.overlap: {name} already has a temporary share of {share} for {days}, and two can’t share a day. Choose other days, or remove that one first.
tasks.title: Tasks
tasks.name: What needs doing
tasks.duration: How long it takes, in minutes
tasks.start-hint: The next times follow from this day.
tasks.on-miss: If it isn’t done in time
tasks.roll-over: It moves on to the next week
tasks.lapse: It’s dropped: the moment has passed
tasks.invalid-name: Enter what needs doing, up to 100 characters.
tasks.invalid-duration: Enter the minutes it takes, a whole number from {min} to {max}.
tasks.invalid-start: Choose a day from today up to a year from now.
tasks.invalid-on-miss: Choose what happens if it isn’t done in time.
tasks.since-last-done: Counted from when it was last done
tasks.first-due-hint: The first time it’s due. After that, it’s counted from when it was last done.

match.countPlural=one: About every day, counted from when it was last done
match.countPlural=other: About every {count} days, counted from when it was last done

match.countPlural=one: About every week, counted from when it was last done
match.countPlural=other: About every {count} weeks, counted from when it was last done

match.countPlural=one: About every month, counted from when it was last done
match.countPlural=other: About every {count} months, counted from when it was last done

tasks.invalid-every-count: Enter how many, a whole number from 1 up to a year: 365 days, 52 weeks or 12 months.
tasks.window-hint: Around each date. For bins collected on a Wednesday morning: from the day before at 18:00 to the day itself at 07:00.
tasks.invalid-when: Choose whether it’s done any time that week or at set times.
tasks.invalid-window: Choose when it starts and ends, within 3 days of its date. It must end after it starts.
schedule.rules-hint: Up to 5. The task happens on every date a rule gives.
schedule.kind-months: Every few months, on the day of the first date
schedule.kind-weekdays-of-month: Every few months, on a weekday of the month
schedule.kind-year: Every year, on the day of the first date
schedule.every: Every how many weeks or months
schedule.start-hint: Every few months and every year repeat on the day of the first date.
schedule.extra-dates-hint: Days it happens as well, such as a collection moved by a holiday.
schedule.exception-dates-hint: Days it doesn't happen, even when a rule gives them.
schedule.add-exception: Add a date to leave out
tasks.invalid-rules: Give up to 5 rules, each every 1 to 52 weeks or 1 to 12 months, on at least one day, with a first date from today up to a year from now. Add a rule or an extra date.
tasks.invalid-extra-dates: Give up to 50 extra dates, each once, from today up to two years from now.
tasks.invalid-exception-dates: Give up to 50 dates to leave out, each once, from today up to two years from now.
tasks.shared-note: Same dates as {tasks}. New dates change theirs too.
tasks.own-dates: Give it dates of its own instead, leaving theirs as they are
tasks.invalid-shared-with: Choose a task on a schedule whose dates it shares.
task.who-hint: Only heads see this. A change counts from the next plan.
task.minimum-age-hint: Leave it empty for any age. Children below it don't get the task, unless you allow it below.
tasks.invalid-minimum-age: Give an age from 1 to 17, or leave it empty.
tasks.invalid-constraints: Choose who does it for each member of the household.
task.linked-to: Whoever does it also does the next
task.linked-to-hint: Such as bringing the bins back in after putting them out.
tasks.invalid-linked-to: Choose another task of the household that isn't a one-off, or none.
areas.title: Areas
areas.intro: Areas group the tasks, such as the kitchen or the garden. They don't change who does what.
areas.name: Name
areas.removed: {name} is removed. Its tasks have no area now.
areas.invalid: Give a name of 1 to 50 characters.
areas.taken: Another area already has that name.
tasks.invalid-area: Choose one of the household's areas, or none.
comparisons.title: What’s hard for you
comparisons.why: The app learns which tasks each of you finds hard, so plans can give each task to whoever minds it least. Nobody else sees your answers, not even the household’s heads.
comparisons.question: Which is harder for you?
comparisons.answered: Saved: {harder} is harder for you than {easier}.
comparisons.changed: The tasks may have changed in the meantime. Here’s a new question.
comparisons.none: There’s nothing to compare yet. Once your household has at least two tasks, you can say here which ones you find harder.
comparisons.order: What’s hard for you, hardest first
comparisons.order-none: Once you’ve answered a question, you’ll see your tasks here, from the hardest for you to the easiest.
comparisons.order-hint: The higher a task is here, the more it counts when plans share out the work. Your answers move tasks up or down.
tasks.add-one-off-intro: For something that needs doing once, such as fixing a shelf. Everyone in the household can add one.
tasks.one-off-date-hint: It’s planned in the week of this day.
tasks.one-off-deadline-hint: Leave it empty to have it done that week. With a day, it can be planned in any week up to it.
tasks.add-one-off-failed: Adding the one-off task didn’t work
tasks.invalid-deadline: Choose a day on or after its day, up to a year from now, or leave it empty.
task.title: Edit the task
task.conflict: This task changed a moment ago, so your changes weren’t saved. They’re still in the form: compare them with the task now, then save again.
task.invalid-start: Keep the day it already has, or choose one from today up to a year from now.
task.remove-intro: It goes from the household’s tasks for good. To have it again, add it as a new task.
task.remove-conflict: This task changed a moment ago, so it wasn’t removed. Check it as it is now, then remove it if you still want to.
task.invalid-deadline: Keep the day it already has, or choose one on or after its day, up to a year from now.
task.remove-one-off-intro: It goes from the household’s tasks for good, and the activity log says you removed it.
availability.title: Who’s away
availability.intro: Plan the days you’re away, so the chores are shared among those at home. Everyone in the household sees these dates, never a reason or a place.
availability.already-removed: Those days away were already removed.
availability.add-failed: Adding the days away didn’t work
availability.invalid-first-day: Choose a first day from today up to a year from now.
availability.invalid-last-day: Choose a last day on or after the first day, up to a year from now.
availability.household-intro: For when everyone is away together, such as a family holiday. Weeks spent entirely away get no plan, chores that fall while you’re all away are skipped, balances don’t change and nobody gets reminders. Only heads plan this.
plan.title: Plan
plan.intro: Who does what, week by week. Each task says why it went to whoever has it.
plan.none: There’s no plan to show yet.
plan.draft: This is a draft. Only heads see it until it’s published on {when}.
plan.published: The plan is published: everyone in the household sees it now.
plan.changed: The draft changed since you opened it. Check it, then publish again.
plan.gone: There’s no draft to publish any more.
plan.any-time: Each task can be done any day of its week.
plan.unassigned-intro: If one is still not given to anyone when the plan is published, it moves on to the next week or is dropped, as its task says. Nobody’s balance is charged for it.
plan.reason.lowest-relative-load: {name} had the least to do so far, for their share.
plan.reason.lowest-relative-load-you: You had the least to do so far, for your share.
plan.reason.only-eligible: {name} was the only one who could do it then.
plan.reason.only-eligible-you: You were the only one who could do it then.
plan.reason.catching-up: It evens out the weeks before.
plan.reason.assigned-by-head-you: A head gave it to you.
plan.reason.linked: It goes with a task {name} had just before.
plan.reason.linked-you: It goes with a task you had just before.
plan.cause.nobody-eligible: Nobody can do it then: everyone is away, or not allowed to do it.
plan.cause.bound-member-not-eligible: The person it always goes to can’t do it then.
plan.cause.linked-member-not-eligible: Whoever had the task it goes with can’t do it then.
plan.add-one-off: Add a one-off task for this week
household.start-intro: Once everyone and the tasks are in, start the household: it then gets a plan every week.
household.started: Your household has started. Its first plan is for the week from {week}: you can check its draft from {draft}, and everyone sees it from {publish}.
activity.set-before-start: Set before the start: shares for {shares}; days away for {daysAway}.
activity.set-before-start-shares: Set before the start: shares for {shares}.
activity.set-before-start-days-away: Set before the start: days away for {daysAway}.
plan.draft-heads-publish: This is a draft. Only heads see it until one of them publishes it.
start.title: Start your household
start.intro: Once your household starts, it gets a plan every week that shares the tasks fairly. Choose when the first one is for.
start.when: When do you want to start?
start.now-hint: This week is planned right away, from today to {last}. Tasks due before today are left out, and the work is shared over the days left. You check the draft, then publish it so everyone sees it.
start.week-start-hint: The first plan is for the full week from that day. You can check its draft from {draft}; everyone sees it from {publish}.
start.already-started: Someone else started the household just now, so nothing changed.

balances.title: Balances
balances.intro: A balance compares what someone did with their fair portion of the household’s work, in points. Positive means ahead of their fair portion, negative means behind.
balances.evening-out: The next weeks’ plans even balances out: whoever is behind gets a little more to do, whoever is ahead a little less.
balances.rate-fast: This household evens them out fast: within two or three weeks.
balances.rate-normal: This household evens them out at a normal pace: over about a month.
balances.rate-slow: This household evens them out slowly: over a season.
balances.no-history: Nothing yet: a week counts once it’s over.

plan.redrafted: The draft is made again, with everyone in the household.
plan.redraft-gone: This draft can’t be made again any more: it was published in the meantime.

match.who=to-you: {actor} planned a temporary share for you.
match.who=yourself: You planned a temporary share for yourself.
